title: The Starry Night
description: The Starry Night is an oil-on-canvas painting by the Dutch Post-Impressionist painter Vincent van Gogh. Painted in June 1889, it depicts the view from the east-facing window of his asylum room at Saint-Rémy-de-Provence, just before sunrise, with the addition of an imaginary village.
source_attribution: Wikimedia Commons — public domain (via Wikipedia: The Starry Night)

title: Mona Lisa
description: The Mona Lisa is a half-length portrait painting by the Italian artist Leonardo da Vinci.
source_attribution: Wikimedia Commons — public domain (via Wikipedia: Mona Lisa)

title: The Great Wave off Kanagawa
description: The Great Wave off Kanagawa (Japanese: 神奈川沖浪裏, Hepburn: Kanagawa-oki Nami Ura; lit. 'Under the Wave off Kanagawa') is a woodblock print by the Japanese ukiyo-e artist Hokusai (1760–1849), created in late 1831 during the Edo period of Japanese history.
source_attribution: Wikimedia Commons — public domain (via Wikipedia: The Great Wave off Kanagawa)

title: Girl with a Pearl Earring
description: Girl with a Pearl Earring (Dutch: Meisje met de parel) is an oil painting by Dutch Golden Age painter Johannes Vermeer, dated c. 1665. Going by various names over the centuries, it acquired its present title towards the end of the 20th century.
source_attribution: Wikimedia Commons — public domain (via Wikipedia: Girl with a Pearl Earring)

title: The Birth of Venus
description: The Birth of Venus (Italian: Nascita di Venere [ˈnaʃʃita di ˈvɛːnere]) is a painting by the Italian artist Sandro Botticelli, probably executed in the mid-1480s. It depicts the goddess Venus arriving at the shore after her birth, when she had emerged from the sea fully grown (called Venus Anadyomene and often depicted in art).
source_attribution: Wikimedia Commons — public domain (via Wikipedia: The Birth of Venus)

title: Impression, Sunrise
description: Impression, Sunrise (French: Impression, soleil levant) is an 1872 painting by Claude Monet first shown at what would become known as the "Exhibition of the Impressionists" in Paris in April, 1874.
source_attribution: Wikimedia Commons — public domain (via Wikipedia: Impression, Sunrise)

title: The Kiss
medium: Oil and gold leaf on canvas
description: The Kiss (German: Der Kuss) is an oil-on-canvas painting with added gold leaf, silver and platinum by the Austrian Symbolist painter Gustav Klimt. It was painted at some point in 1907 and 1908, during the height of what scholars call his "Golden Period".
source_attribution: Wikimedia Commons — public domain (via Wikipedia: The Kiss (Klimt))

title: Water Lilies
description: Water Lilies (French: Nymphéas [nɛ̃.fe.a]) is a series of approximately 250 oil paintings by French Impressionist Claude Monet (1840–1926). The paintings depict his flower garden at his home in Giverny, and were the main focus of his artistic production during the last 31 years of his life.
source_attribution: Wikimedia Commons — public domain (via Wikipedia: Water Lilies (Monet series))

title: Las Meninas
description: Las Meninas (Spanish: [las meˈninas]; Spanish for 'The Ladies-in-waiting') is a 1656 oil painting in the Museo del Prado in Madrid, by Diego Velázquez, the leading artist in the court of King Philip IV of Spain and Portugal, and of the Spanish Golden Age.
source_attribution: Wikimedia Commons — public domain (via Wikipedia: Las Meninas)

title: The Scream
medium: Oil, tempera and pastel on cardboard
description: The Scream is an art composition created by Norwegian artist Edvard Munch in 1893. The Norwegian name of the piece is Skrik ('Scream'), and the German title under which it was first exhibited is Der Schrei der Natur ('The Scream of Nature').
source_attribution: Wikimedia Commons — public domain (via Wikipedia: The Scream)

title: A Sunday on La Grande Jatte
description: A Sunday Afternoon on the Island of La Grande Jatte (French: Un dimanche après-midi à l'Île de la Grande Jatte) was painted from 1884 to 1886 and is Georges Seurat's most famous work.
source_attribution: Wikimedia Commons — public domain (via Wikipedia: A Sunday Afternoon on the Island of La Grande Jatte)

title: Starry Night Over the Rhône
description: Starry Night   (September 1888, French: La Nuit étoilée), commonly known as Starry Night Over the Rhône, is a Vincent van Gogh painting of the night sky in Arles. It was painted on the bank of the Rhône, only a one or two-minute walk from the Yellow House, which van Gogh was renting at the time.
source_attribution: Wikimedia Commons — public domain (via Wikipedia: Starry Night Over the Rhône)

title: The Night Watch
description: Militia Company of District II under the Command of Captain Frans Banninck Cocq, also known as The Shooting Company of Frans Banning Cocq and Willem van Ruytenburch, but commonly referred to as The Night Watch (Dutch: De Nachtwacht), is a 1642 painting by Rembrandt van Rijn.
source_attribution: Wikimedia Commons — public domain (via Wikipedia: The Night Watch)

title: The Anatomy Lesson of Dr. Nicolaes Tulp
description: The Anatomy Lesson of Dr. Nicolaes Tulp is a 1632 oil painting on canvas by Rembrandt housed in the Mauritshuis museum in The Hague, Netherlands. It was originally created to be displayed by the Surgeons Guild in their meeting room.
source_attribution: Wikimedia Commons — public domain (via Wikipedia: The Anatomy Lesson of Dr. Nicolaes Tulp)

title: The Garden of Earthly Delights
description: The Garden of Earthly Delights (Dutch: De tuin der lusten, lit. 'The garden of lusts') is the modern title given to a five-panel triptych (three oil-painted panels when open, two oak panels when closed) by the Early Netherlandish master Hieronymus Bosch, between 1490 and 1510, when Bosch was between 40 and 60 years old.
source_attribution: Wikimedia Commons — public domain (via Wikipedia: The Garden of Earthly Delights)

title: The Tower of Babel
description: The Tower of Babel was the subject of two surviving paintings and one lost painting by Dutch and Flemish Renaissance painter Pieter Bruegel the Elder. The earliest of the three, a miniature painted on ivory, was completed in 1552–1553 while Bruegel was in Rome, and is now lost.
source_attribution: Wikimedia Commons — public domain (via Wikipedia: The Tower of Babel (Bruegel))

title: The Hunters in the Snow
description: The Hunters in the Snow (Dutch: Jagers in de Sneeuw), also known as The Return of the Hunters, is a 1565 oil-on-wood painting by Pieter Bruegel the Elder. The Northern Renaissance work is one of a series of works, five of which still survive, that depict different times of the year.
source_attribution: Wikimedia Commons — public domain (via Wikipedia: The Hunters in the Snow)

title: The Arnolfini Portrait
description: The Arnolfini Portrait (or The Arnolfini Wedding, The Arnolfini Marriage, the Portrait of Giovanni Arnolfini and his Wife, or other titles) is an oil painting on oak panel by the Early Netherlandish painter Jan van Eyck, dated 1434 and now in the National Gallery, London.
source_attribution: Wikimedia Commons — public domain (via Wikipedia: The Arnolfini Portrait)

title: The Creation of Adam
description: The Creation of Adam (Italian: Creazione di Adamo), also known as The Creation of Man, is a fresco painting by Italian artist Michelangelo, which forms part of the Sistine Chapel's ceiling, painted 1508–1512.
source_attribution: Wikimedia Commons — public domain (via Wikipedia: The Creation of Adam)

title: The School of Athens
description: The School of Athens (Italian: Scuola di Atene) is a fresco by the Italian Renaissance artist Raphael. It was painted between 1509 and 1511 as part of a commission by Pope Julius II to decorate the rooms now called the Stanze di Raffaello in the Apostolic Palace in Vatican City.
source_attribution: Wikimedia Commons — public domain (via Wikipedia: The School of Athens)

title: The Last Supper
description: The Last Supper (Italian: Il Cenacolo [il tʃeˈnaːkolo] or L'Ultima Cena [ˈlultima ˈtʃeːna]) is a mural painting by the Italian High Renaissance artist Leonardo da Vinci, dated to c. 1495–1498, housed in the refectory of the Convent of Santa Maria delle Grazie in Milan, Italy.
source_attribution: Wikimedia Commons — public domain (via Wikipedia: The Last Supper (Leonardo))

title: Primavera
description: Primavera (Italian pronunciation: [primaˈvɛːra], meaning "Spring") is a large panel painting in tempera paint by the Italian Renaissance painter Sandro Botticelli made in the late 1470s or early 1480s (datings vary).
source_attribution: Wikimedia Commons — public domain (via Wikipedia: Primavera (Botticelli))

title: The Calling of Saint Matthew
description: The Calling of Saint Matthew is an oil painting by the Italian Baroque master Caravaggio that depicts the moment Jesus Christ calls on the tax collector Matthew to follow him. It was completed in 1599–1600 for the Contarelli Chapel in the church of the French congregation, San Luigi dei Francesi in Rome, where it remains.
source_attribution: Wikimedia Commons — public domain (via Wikipedia: The Calling of St Matthew (Caravaggio))

title: Judith Slaying Holofernes
description: Judith Slaying Holofernes is a painting by the Italian early Baroque artist Artemisia Gentileschi, completed in 1612–13 and now at the Museo Capodimonte, Naples, Italy. The picture is considered one of her iconic works.
source_attribution: Wikimedia Commons — public domain (via Wikipedia: Judith Slaying Holofernes (Artemisia Gentileschi, Naples))

title: The Third of May 1808
description: The Third of May 1808 in Madrid (commonly known as The Third of May 1808) and also known, in Spanish, as El tres de mayo de 1808 en Madrid or Los fusilamientos de la montaña del Príncipe Pío, or Los fusilamientos del tres de mayo, is a painting completed in 1814 by the Spanish painter Francisco Goya.
source_attribution: Wikimedia Commons — public domain (via Wikipedia: The Third of May 1808)

title: Saturn Devouring His Son
medium: Mixed media mural transferred to canvas
description: Saturn Devouring His Son (Spanish: Saturno devorando a su hijo; also known as Saturn) is a painting by Spanish artist Francisco Goya. The work is one of the 14 so-called Black Paintings that Goya painted directly on the walls of his house some time between 1820 and 1823.
source_attribution: Wikimedia Commons — public domain (via Wikipedia: Saturn Devouring His Son)

title: Liberty Leading the People
description: Liberty Leading the People (French: La Liberté guidant le peuple [la libɛʁte ɡidɑ̃ lə pœpl]) is a painting of the Romantic era by the French artist Eugène Delacroix,  commemorating the July Revolution of 1830 that toppled King Charles X (r.
source_attribution: Wikimedia Commons — public domain (via Wikipedia: Liberty Leading the People)

title: The Raft of the Medusa
description: The Raft of the Medusa (French: Le Radeau de la Méduse [lə ʁado d(ə) la medyz])—originally titled Scène de Naufrage (Shipwreck Scene)—is an oil painting of 1818–1819 by the French Romantic painter and lithographer Théodore Géricault (1791–1824).
source_attribution: Wikimedia Commons — public domain (via Wikipedia: The Raft of the Medusa)

title: Wanderer above the Sea of Fog
description: Wanderer above the Sea of Fog is a painting by German Romanticist artist Caspar David Friedrich in 1818.
source_attribution: Wikimedia Commons — public domain (via Wikipedia: Wanderer above the Sea of Fog)

title: The Fighting Temeraire
description: The Fighting Temeraire, tugged to her last berth to be broken up, 1838 is an oil-on-canvas painting by the English artist Joseph Mallord William Turner, painted in 1838 and exhibited at the Royal Academy in 1839.
source_attribution: Wikimedia Commons — public domain (via Wikipedia: The Fighting Temeraire)

title: Rain, Steam and Speed
description: Rain, Steam, and Speed – The Great Western Railway is an oil painting by the 19th-century British painter J. M. W. Turner. The painting was first exhibited at the Royal Academy in 1844, though it may have been painted earlier.
source_attribution: Wikimedia Commons — public domain (via Wikipedia: Rain, Steam and Speed – The Great Western Railway)

title: The Hay Wain
description: The Hay Wain – originally titled Landscape: Noon – is a painting by John Constable, completed in 1821, which depicts a rural scene on the River Stour between the English counties of Suffolk and Essex.
source_attribution: Wikimedia Commons — public domain (via Wikipedia: The Hay Wain)

title: The Lady of Shalott
description: The Lady of Shalott is a painting of 1888 by the English painter John William Waterhouse. It is a representation of the ending of Alfred, Lord Tennyson's 1832 poem of the same name.
source_attribution: Wikimedia Commons — public domain (via Wikipedia: The Lady of Shalott (painting))

title: Proserpine
description: Proserpine (also Proserpina or Persephone) is an oil painting on canvas by British Pre-Raphaelite artist and poet Dante Gabriel Rossetti. It was made in 1874 and is now in the collection of the Tate Britain.
source_attribution: Wikimedia Commons — public domain (via Wikipedia: Proserpine (Rossetti painting))

title: The Gleaners
description: The Gleaners (Des glaneuses) is an oil painting by Jean-François Millet completed in 1857. It is held in the Musée d'Orsay, in Paris. It depicts three peasant women gleaning a field of stray stalks of wheat after the harvest.
source_attribution: Wikimedia Commons — public domain (via Wikipedia: The Gleaners)

title: The Angelus
description: The Angelus (French: L'Angélus) is an oil painting by French painter Jean-François Millet, completed between 1857 and 1859. The painting depicts two peasants in a field bowing over a basket of potatoes, while saying a prayer, the Angelus.
source_attribution: Wikimedia Commons — public domain (via Wikipedia: The Angelus (painting))

title: A Burial at Ornans
description: A Burial at Ornans (French: Un enterrement à Ornans, also known as A Funeral at Ornans) is a painting of 1849–50 by Gustave Courbet. It is widely regarded as a major turning point in 19th-century French art.
source_attribution: Wikimedia Commons — public domain (via Wikipedia: A Burial At Ornans)

title: Olympia
description: Olympia is an 1863 oil painting by Édouard Manet, depicting a nude white woman ("Olympia") lying on a bed being attended to by a black maid. The French government acquired the painting in 1890 after a public subscription organized by Claude Monet.
source_attribution: Wikimedia Commons — public domain (via Wikipedia: Olympia (Manet))

title: Le Déjeuner sur l'herbe
description: Le Déjeuner sur l'herbe (French: [lə deʒœne syʁ lɛʁb, -ʒøn-]; The Luncheon on the Grass) – originally titled Le Bain (The Bath) – is a large  oil on canvas  painting by  Édouard Manet  created in 1862 and 1863.
source_attribution: Wikimedia Commons — public domain (via Wikipedia: Le Déjeuner sur l'herbe)

title: A Bar at the Folies-Bergère
description: A Bar at the Folies-Bergère (French: Un bar aux Folies Bergère) is a painting by Édouard Manet, considered to be his last major work. It was painted in 1882 and exhibited at the Paris Salon of that year.
source_attribution: Wikimedia Commons — public domain (via Wikipedia: A Bar at the Folies-Bergère)

title: L'Absinthe
description: L'Absinthe (English: The Absinthe Drinker or Glass of Absinthe) is a painting by Edgar Degas, painted between 1875 and 1876. Its original title was Dans un Café, a name often used today.
source_attribution: Wikimedia Commons — public domain (via Wikipedia: L'Absinthe)

title: Bal du moulin de la Galette
description: Bal du moulin de la Galette (commonly known as Dance at Le moulin de la Galette) is an 1876 painting by French artist Pierre-Auguste Renoir. It is housed at the Musée d'Orsay in Paris and is one of Impressionism's most celebrated masterpieces.
source_attribution: Wikimedia Commons — public domain (via Wikipedia: Bal du moulin de la Galette)

title: Luncheon of the Boating Party
description: Luncheon of the Boating Party (French: Le Déjeuner des canotiers) is an 1880–1881 painting by French impressionist Pierre-Auguste Renoir. Exhibited at the Seventh Impressionist Exhibition in 1882, it was identified as the best painting in the show by three critics.
source_attribution: Wikimedia Commons — public domain (via Wikipedia: Luncheon of the Boating Party)

title: Rouen Cathedral series
description: The Rouen Cathedral series was painted in the 1890s by French impressionist Claude Monet. The paintings in the series each capture the façade of Rouen Cathedral at different times of the day and year and reflect changes in its appearance under different lighting conditions..
source_attribution: Wikimedia Commons — public domain (via Wikipedia: Rouen Cathedral (Monet series))

title: Woman with a Parasol
description: Woman with a Parasol – Madame Monet and Her Son is an oil-on-canvas painting by Claude Monet from 1875. The Impressionist work depicts his wife Camille Monet and their son Jean Monet in the period from 1871 to 1877 while they were living in Argenteuil, capturing a moment on a stroll on a windy summer's day.
source_attribution: Wikimedia Commons — public domain (via Wikipedia: Woman with a Parasol – Madame Monet and Her Son)

title: The Child's Bath
description: The Child's Bath (or The Bath) is an 1893 oil painting by American artist Mary Cassatt. The painting continues her interest in depicting bathing and motherhood, but it is distinct in its angle of vision.
source_attribution: Wikimedia Commons — public domain (via Wikipedia: The Child's Bath)

title: The Cradle
description: The Cradle  is an oil on canvas painting by the French Impressionist painter Berthe Morisot, executed in 1872. It is on display at the Musée d'Orsay in Paris..
source_attribution: Wikimedia Commons — public domain (via Wikipedia: The Cradle (Morisot))

title: The Card Players
description: The Card Players is a series of oil paintings by the French Post-Impressionist artist Paul Cézanne. Painted during Cézanne's final period in the early 1890s, there are five paintings in the series.
source_attribution: Wikimedia Commons — public domain (via Wikipedia: The Card Players)

title: Mont Sainte-Victoire
description: Mont Sainte-Victoire is a series of oil paintings by French artist Paul Cézanne, depicting the French mountain Montagne Sainte-Victoire in Provence..
source_attribution: Wikimedia Commons — public domain (via Wikipedia: Mont Sainte-Victoire (Cézanne))

title: Sunflowers
description: Sunflowers (original title, in French: Tournesols) is the title of two series of still life paintings by the Dutch painter Vincent van Gogh. The first series, executed in Paris in 1887, depicts the flowers lying on the ground, while the second set, made a year later in Arles, shows a bouquet of sunflowers in a vase.
source_attribution: Wikimedia Commons — public domain (via Wikipedia: Sunflowers (Van Gogh series))

title: Café Terrace at Night
description: Café Terrace at Night is an 1888 oil painting by the Dutch artist Vincent van Gogh. It is also known as The Cafe Terrace on the Place du Forum, and, when first exhibited in 1891, was entitled Coffeehouse, in the evening (Café, le soir).
source_attribution: Wikimedia Commons — public domain (via Wikipedia: Café Terrace at Night)

title: Bedroom in Arles
description: Bedroom in Arles (French: La Chambre à Arles; Dutch: Slaapkamer te Arles) is the title given to three similar paintings by 19th-century Dutch Post-Impressionist painter Vincent van Gogh.
source_attribution: Wikimedia Commons — public domain (via Wikipedia: Bedroom in Arles)

title: Wheatfield with Crows
description: Wheatfield with Crows (Dutch: Korenveld met kraaien) is a July 1890 painting by Vincent van Gogh. It has been cited by several critics as one of his greatest works. It is commonly stated that this was Van Gogh's final painting.
source_attribution: Wikimedia Commons — public domain (via Wikipedia: Wheatfield with Crows)

title: Where Do We Come From?
description: Where Do We Come From? What Are We? Where Are We Going? (French: D'où venons-nous ? Que sommes-nous ? Où allons-nous ?) is an 1897–98 painting by French artist Paul Gauguin. The painting was created in Tahiti and is in the Museum of Fine Arts in Boston, Massachusetts.
source_attribution: Wikimedia Commons — public domain (via Wikipedia: Where Do We Come From? What Are We? Where Are We Going?)

title: Vision after the Sermon
description: Vision after the Sermon (Jacob Wrestling with the Angel) is an oil painting by French artist Paul Gauguin, completed in 1888. It is now in the Scottish National Gallery, Edinburgh. It depicts a scene from the Bible in which Jacob wrestles an angel.
source_attribution: Wikimedia Commons — public domain (via Wikipedia: Vision after the Sermon)

title: At the Moulin Rouge
description: At the Moulin Rouge (French: Au Moulin Rouge) is an oil-on-canvas painting by French artist Henri de Toulouse-Lautrec. It was painted between 1892 and 1895. Included in the background is a self-portrait of the artist in profile.
source_attribution: Wikimedia Commons — public domain (via Wikipedia: At the Moulin Rouge)

title: The Sleeping Gypsy
description: The Sleeping Gypsy  (French: La Bohémienne endormie) is an 1897 oil on canvas painting by the French Naïve artist Henri Rousseau (1844–1910). It is a fantastical depiction of a lion musing over a sleeping woman on a moonlit night.
source_attribution: Wikimedia Commons — public domain (via Wikipedia: The Sleeping Gypsy)

title: The Dream
description: The Dream (French: Le Rêve; occasionally also known as Le Songe or Rêve exotique) is a large oil-on-canvas painting created by Henri Rousseau in 1910, one of more than 25 Rousseau paintings with a jungle theme.
source_attribution: Wikimedia Commons — public domain (via Wikipedia: The Dream (Rousseau painting))

title: Whistler's Mother
description: Arrangement in Grey and Black No. 1, best known under its colloquial name Whistler's Mother or Portrait of Artist's Mother, is a painting in oils on canvas created by the American-born painter James McNeill Whistler in 1871.
source_attribution: Wikimedia Commons — public domain (via Wikipedia: Whistler's Mother)

title: Nocturne in Black and Gold
description: Nocturne in Black and Gold – The Falling Rocket is a c. 1875 painting by James McNeill Whistler held in the Detroit Institute of Arts. The painting exemplified the art for art's sake movement – a concept formulated by Pierre Jules Théophile Gautier and Charles Baudelaire.
source_attribution: Wikimedia Commons — public domain (via Wikipedia: Nocturne in Black and Gold – The Falling Rocket)

title: Portrait of Madame X
description: Madame X or Portrait of Madame X is an 1884 portrait painting by John Singer Sargent of a young socialite, Virginie Amélie Avegno Gautreau, wife of the French banker Pierre Gautreau.
source_attribution: Wikimedia Commons — public domain (via Wikipedia: Portrait of Madame X)

title: Carnation, Lily, Lily, Rose
description: Carnation, Lily, Lily, Rose is an oil-on-canvas painting made by the American painter John Singer Sargent in 1885–86.
source_attribution: Wikimedia Commons — public domain (via Wikipedia: Carnation, Lily, Lily, Rose)

title: The Gulf Stream
description: The Gulf Stream is an 1899 oil painting by the American artist Winslow Homer. It shows a man in a small dismasted rudderless fishing boat struggling against the storm-tossed waves and perils of the sea, presumably near the Gulf Stream, and was the artist's statement on a theme that had interested him for more than a decade.
source_attribution: Wikimedia Commons — public domain (via Wikipedia: The Gulf Stream (painting))

title: Breezing Up
description: Breezing Up (A Fair Wind) is an oil painting by American artist Winslow Homer. It depicts a catboat called the Gloucester chopping through that city's harbor under "a fair wind" (Homer's original title).
source_attribution: Wikimedia Commons — public domain (via Wikipedia: Breezing Up (A Fair Wind))

title: Portrait of Adele Bloch-Bauer I
medium: Oil, silver and gold on canvas
description: Portrait of Adele Bloch-Bauer I (also called The Lady in Gold or The Woman in Gold) is an oil painting on canvas, with gold leaf, by Gustav Klimt, completed between 1903 and 1907. The portrait was commissioned by the sitter's husband, Ferdinand Bloch-Bauer, a Viennese and Jewish banker and sugar producer.
source_attribution: Wikimedia Commons — public domain (via Wikipedia: Portrait of Adele Bloch-Bauer I)

title: Death and Life
description: Death and Life (German: Tod und Leben) is an oil-on-canvas painting by Austrian painter Gustav Klimt. The painting was started in 1908 and completed in 1915. It depicts an allegorical subject in Art Nouveau style.
source_attribution: Wikimedia Commons — public domain (via Wikipedia: Death and Life (Klimt))

title: Portrait of Wally
description: Portrait of Wally is a 1912 oil painting by Austrian painter Egon Schiele of Walburga "Wally" Neuzil, a woman whom he met in 1911 when he was 21 and she was 17. She became his lover and model for several years, depicted in a number of Schiele's most striking paintings.
source_attribution: Wikimedia Commons — public domain (via Wikipedia: Portrait of Wally)

title: On White II
description: Auf Weiss II (Sur blanc II), in English: On White II, is a 1923 oil-on-canvas painting by Russian painter Wassily Kandinsky. It was created when the artist was a teacher at the Bauhaus in Weimar.
source_attribution: Wikimedia Commons — public domain (via Wikipedia: On White II)

title: Black Square
description: Black Square (Russian: Чёрный квадрат) is a 1915 oil on linen canvas painting by the Russian avant-garde artist and theorist Kazimir Malevich. There are four painted versions, the first of which was completed in 1915 and described by the artist as his breakthrough work and the inception of his Suprematist art movement (1915–1919).
source_attribution: Wikimedia Commons — public domain (via Wikipedia: Black Square (painting))

title: Senecio
description: Senecio or Head of a Man Going Senile is an oil on canvas mounted on panel Cubist painting by Swiss artist Paul Klee, from 1922. It is held in the Kunstmuseum Basel..
source_attribution: Wikimedia Commons — public domain (via Wikipedia: Senecio (Klee))

title: Twittering Machine
description: Twittering Machine (Die Zwitscher-Maschine) is a 1922 watercolor with gouache, pen-and-ink, and oil transfer on paper by Swiss-German painter Paul Klee. Like other artworks by Klee, it blends biology and machinery, depicting a loosely sketched group of birds on a wire or branch connected to a hand-crank.
source_attribution: Wikimedia Commons — public domain (via Wikipedia: Twittering Machine)

title: Fine Wind, Clear Morning (Red Fuji)
description: Fine Wind, Clear Morning (Japanese: 凱風快晴, Hepburn: Gaifū kaisei; literally South Wind, Clear Sky), also known as Red Fuji (赤富士, Akafuji), is a woodblock print by Japanese artist Hokusai (1760–1849), part of his Thirty-six Views of Mount Fuji series, dating from c. 1830 to 1832.
source_attribution: Wikimedia Commons — public domain (via Wikipedia: Red Fuji)

title: Ivan the Terrible and His Son Ivan
description: Ivan the Terrible and His Son Ivan on 16 November 1581 is a painting by Russian realist artist Ilya Repin made between 1883 and 1885. It depicts the grief-stricken Russian tsar Ivan the Terrible cradling his dying son, the Tsarevich Ivan Ivanovich, shortly after Ivan the Terrible had dealt a fatal blow to his son's head in a fit of anger.
source_attribution: Wikimedia Commons — public domain (via Wikipedia: Ivan the Terrible and His Son Ivan)

title: Barge Haulers on the Volga
description: Barge Haulers on the Volga or Burlaki (Russian: Бурлаки на Волге, Burlaki na Volge) is an 1870–1873 oil-on-canvas painting by Russian realist artist Ilya Repin. It depicts 11 men (burlaki) hauling a barge along the banks of the Volga River.
source_attribution: Wikimedia Commons — public domain (via Wikipedia: Barge Haulers on the Volga)

title: The Swing
description: The Swing (French: L'Escarpolette), also known as The Happy Accidents of the Swing (French: Les Hasards heureux de l'escarpolette, the original title), is an 18th-century oil painting by Jean-Honoré Fragonard in the Wallace Collection in London.
source_attribution: Wikimedia Commons — public domain (via Wikipedia: The Swing (Fragonard))

title: Pilgrimage to Cythera
description: The Embarkation for Cythera ("L'embarquement pour Cythère") is a painting by the French painter Jean-Antoine Watteau. It is also known as Voyage to Cythera and Pilgrimage to the Isle of Cythera.
source_attribution: Wikimedia Commons — public domain (via Wikipedia: Pilgrimage to Cythera)

title: The Death of Marat
description: The Death of Marat (French: La Mort de Marat or Marat Assassiné) is a 1793 painting by Jacques-Louis David depicting the artist's friend and murdered French revolutionary leader, Jean-Paul Marat.
source_attribution: Wikimedia Commons — public domain (via Wikipedia: The Death of Marat)

title: Oath of the Horatii
description: Oath of the Horatii (French: Le Serment des Horaces) is a large painting by the French artist Jacques-Louis David painted in 1784 and 1785 and now on display in the Louvre in Paris.
source_attribution: Wikimedia Commons — public domain (via Wikipedia: Oath of the Horatii)

title: La Grande Odalisque
description: Grande Odalisque, also known as Une Odalisque or La Grande Odalisque, is an oil painting by Jean-Auguste-Dominique Ingres depicting an odalisque, or concubine in 1814. Ingres' contemporaries considered the work to signify Ingres' break from Neoclassicism, indicating a shift toward exotic Romanticism.
source_attribution: Wikimedia Commons — public domain (via Wikipedia: La Grande Odalisque)

title: Venus of Urbino
description: The Venus of Urbino (also known as Reclining Venus) is an oil painting by Italian painter Titian, depicting a nude young woman, traditionally identified with the goddess Venus, reclining on a couch or bed in the sumptuous surroundings of a Renaissance palace.
source_attribution: Wikimedia Commons — public domain (via Wikipedia: Venus of Urbino)

title: The Ambassadors
description: The Ambassadors is a 1533 painting by Hans Holbein the Younger. Also known as Jean de Dinteville and Georges de Selve, after the two people it portrays, it was created in the Tudor period, in the same year Elizabeth I was born.
source_attribution: Wikimedia Commons — public domain (via Wikipedia: The Ambassadors (Holbein))

title: Self-Portrait at 28
description: Self-Portrait (or Self-Portrait at Twenty-Eight) is a panel painting by the German Renaissance artist Albrecht Dürer. Completed early in 1500, just before his 29th birthday, it is the last of his three painted self-portraits.
source_attribution: Wikimedia Commons — public domain (via Wikipedia: Self-Portrait (Dürer, Munich))

title: View of Toledo
description: View of Toledo (Spanish: Vista de Toledo), is one of the two surviving landscapes painted by El Greco, along with View and Plan of Toledo. View of Toledo is held by the Metropolitan Museum of Art in New York City.
source_attribution: Wikimedia Commons — public domain (via Wikipedia: View of Toledo)

title: The Milkmaid
description: The Milkmaid (Dutch: De melkmeid or Het melkmeisje), sometimes called The Kitchen Maid (Dutch: De keukenmeid), is an oil-on-canvas painting of a "milkmaid", in fact, a domestic kitchen maid, by the Dutch artist Johannes Vermeer.
source_attribution: Wikimedia Commons — public domain (via Wikipedia: The Milkmaid (Vermeer))

title: View of Delft
description: View of Delft (Dutch: Zicht op Delft) is an oil painting by Johannes Vermeer, painted c. 1659–1661. The painting of the Dutch artist's hometown is among his best known. It is one of three known paintings of Delft by Vermeer, along with The Little Street and the lost painting House Standing in Delft, and his only cityscape.
source_attribution: Wikimedia Commons — public domain (via Wikipedia: View of Delft)

title: Composition with Red, Blue and Yellow
description: Composition with Red, Blue and Yellow is an oil on canvas painting by Piet Mondrian, from 1930..
source_attribution: Wikimedia Commons — public domain (via Wikipedia: Composition with Red Blue and Yellow)

title: Isle of the Dead
description: Isle of the Dead (German: Die Toteninsel) is the best-known painting of Swiss Symbolist artist Arnold Böcklin (1827–1901). Prints were very popular in central Europe in the early 20th century—Vladimir Nabokov observed in his 1936 novel Despair that they could be "found in every Berlin home".
source_attribution: Wikimedia Commons — public domain (via Wikipedia: The Isle of the Dead (painting))

title: The Great Red Dragon
description: The Great Red Dragon paintings are a series of watercolour paintings by the English poet and painter William Blake, created between 1805 and 1810. It was during this period that Blake was commissioned to create over one hundred paintings intended to illustrate books of the Bible.
source_attribution: Wikimedia Commons — public domain (via Wikipedia: The Great Red Dragon Paintings)
